questions.question:
Choose the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to that expressed in the original pair:
**TRACTOR : AGRICULTURE**
questions.solution: A tractor is the primary operational mechanical instrument used by a professional in agriculture, just as a scalpel is the primary surgical instrument used by a surgeon in surgery.

questions.question: Given the premise: "Every agrarian economy depends critically on rainfall." If Province Z is an agrarian economy, which of the following conclusions must be logically valid?

options.A: Province Z depends critically on rainfall
options.B: Province Z receives heavy rainfall throughout the year
options.C: Every economy that depends on rainfall is agrarian
options.D: Province Z has no irrigation infrastructure

questions.solution: This is a direct application of categorical syllogism (Modus Ponens): All A are B. Z is an A. Therefore, Z is B. Hence Province Z depends critically on rainfall.

questions.question: [Figure description: A series of three squares is shown. Square 1 contains one diagonal line drawn from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner. Square 2 contains both diagonals (top-left to bottom-right AND top-right to bottom-left). Square 3 contains both diagonals plus a horizontal line joining the midpoints of the left and right sides. Each square in the series adds exactly one new straight line to all the lines already present in the previous square, and no line already drawn is ever removed.]Which of the following best describes Square 4, the next figure in the series?Figure Q.3 — spatial figure series (squares with increasing internal lines)

options.A: Both diagonals, the horizontal midline, and a vertical line joining the midpoints of the top and bottom sides
options.B: Only a vertical line joining the midpoints of the top and bottom sides
options.C: Both diagonals only, with the horizontal midline removed
options.D: An empty square with no internal lines

questions.question:
Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence:
"The technical committee agreed ________ the proposed alterations to the watershed conservation plan after extensive field deliberation."
questions.solution: In standard English grammar, one agrees *with* a person or opinion, but agrees *to* a proposal, plan, or alteration. Therefore, "agreed to the proposed alterations" is grammatically correct.

questions.question: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'ESOTERIC':
questions.solution: 'Esoteric' describes knowledge intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people. The antonym is 'Familiar'.

questions.question:
Statements:
I. All agronomists are researchers.
II. Some researchers are drone pilots.
Which of the following conclusions can be logically derived beyond doubt?

options.C: At least some researchers are agronomists
options.D: No agronomist is a drone pilot

questions.solution: From Statement I ("All agronomists are researchers"), by immediate conversion (subalternation), "Some researchers are agronomists". Since Statement II only states that some researchers are drone pilots without specifying whether they overlap with the agronomist subset, neither A, B, nor D can be affirmed with certainty. Thus, only C is logically certain.

questions.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence illustrating proper negative inversion from the options below:

options.A: Not only did the harvest fail, but the granary was also destroyed by pests.
options.B: Not only the harvest failed, but the granary was also destroyed by pests.
options.C: Not only did the harvest failed, but the granary was also destroyed by pests.
options.D: The harvest failed not only, but also the granary was destroyed by pests.

questions.solution: When a sentence begins with the negative coordinating correlative "Not only", it triggers subject-auxiliary inversion: "Not only did [auxiliary] + the harvest [subject] + fail [base verb]...". Option A correctly applies this inverted syntax, followed by a balanced independent clause.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question:
"Precision agriculture relies fundamentally on spatial variability mapping. By deploying global positioning systems and multispectral reflectance sensors, variable-rate fertilizer applicators adjust nutrient delivery in real time. Rather than treating an entire field as a homogenous expanse, inputs are localized to match soil fertility deficits, which curtail excess nitrate leaching into subterranean aquifers and enhances input-use efficiency."
Which of the following statements is most directly supported by the passage?

options.A: Precision agriculture eliminates the necessity of soil testing and laboratory analyses entirely.
options.B: Variable-rate fertilizer application treats farm fields as uniform zones to simplify tractor navigation.
options.C: Localizing nutrient application based on spatial variability mitigates groundwater contamination.
options.D: Multispectral sensors increase nitrate leaching by accelerating fertilizer chemical absorption.

questions.solution: The passage explicitly states that inputs are localized to match soil deficits, "which curtail excess nitrate leaching into subterranean aquifers and enhances input-use efficiency." Hence, mitigating groundwater (subterranean aquifer) contamination is directly supported.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question:
"Renewable bioenergy systems often face an energy return on investment (EROI) paradox. While sugarcane bioethanol delivers an EROI exceeding $8:1$, corn-based ethanol exhibits an EROI marginally above unity ($1.2:1$ to $1.5:1$) when energy inputs from tractor diesel, nitrogen synthesis, distillation steam, and transport logistics are comprehensively accounted for. Thus, life-cycle carbon neutrality cannot be assumed merely by virtue of biological feedstock origin."
The author's primary argument in the passage is that:

options.A: All biological feedstocks provide equal thermodynamic advantages over fossil fuels.
options.B: Biofuel sustainability must be assessed through comprehensive life-cycle energy accounting rather than assumed origin.
options.C: Sugarcane bioethanol is thermodynamically unsustainable due to high distillation energy requirements.
options.D: Corn ethanol should replace sugarcane bioethanol due to superior agricultural productivity.

questions.solution: The author contrasts the high EROI of sugarcane with the marginal EROI of corn ethanol when accounting for all upstream inputs, concluding that "life-cycle carbon neutrality cannot be assumed merely by virtue of biological feedstock origin." This directly supports option B.

questions.question:
Consider the argument:
"A regional agricultural cooperative introduced subsidized solar irrigation pumps across a drought-prone district. Two years later, the groundwater table dropped by an alarming $4\text{ metres}$, even though annual rainfall was normal. The cooperative concluded that solar pumps directly caused the water table depletion by eliminating the marginal fuel cost of pumping, thereby incentivizing farmers to pump water continuously."
Which of the following, if true, most strongly WEAKENS the cooperative's conclusion?

options.A: Solar pumps require minimal routine mechanical maintenance compared to diesel engines.
options.B: Concurrently with the solar pump scheme, the regional government mandated a shift from low-water millets to water-intensive sugarcane cultivation across the entire district.
options.C: Farmers with solar pumps reported higher seasonal gross revenues than those operating diesel pumps.
options.D: The photovoltaic panels degraded in energy conversion efficiency by $2\%$ per year due to dust deposition.

questions.solution: To weaken a causal claim ($X \implies Y$), demonstrating an alternative confounding cause that independently accounts for the observed effect is standard. Mandating water-intensive sugarcane across the district directly explains massive groundwater depletion, weakening the claim that solar pumps were the primary culprit.

questions.question: If $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ real skew-symmetric matrix, then the determinant of $A$ is always equal to:
questions.solution:
For any skew-symmetric matrix $A$ of order $n$, $A^T = -A$.
Taking determinants on both sides:
$$\det(A^T) = \det(-A) = (-1)^n \det(A)$$
Since $\det(A^T) = \det(A)$ and here $n = 3$ is odd:
$$\det(A) = -\det(A) \implies 2\det(A) = 0 \implies \det(A) = 0$$
Therefore, the determinant of any odd-order skew-symmetric matrix is always $0$.

questions.question: The Cayley–Hamilton theorem asserts that every square matrix satisfies its own:
questions.solution: The Cayley–Hamilton theorem states that if $p(\lambda) = \det(A - \lambda I) = 0$ is the characteristic equation of an $n \times n$ matrix $A$, then substituting matrix $A$ into $p$ yields $p(A) = 0$, the zero matrix. Thus, every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation.

questions.question: Let $Q$ be a $3 \times 3$ real orthogonal matrix. The determinant of the matrix $(Q^T Q + 3I)$ is ________ (answer in integer).
questions.solution:
For any real orthogonal matrix $Q$, we have $Q^T Q = I$.
Therefore:
$$Q^T Q + 3I = I + 3I = 4I$$
Taking the determinant for a $3 \times 3$ matrix:
$$\det(4I) = 4^3 \det(I) = 64 \times 1 = 64$$

questions.question: A homogeneous system of linear equations $Ax = 0$ has $4$ equations and $6$ unknowns. If the rank of the coefficient matrix $A$ is $3$, the number of linearly independent solutions is:
questions.solution:
By the Rank-Nullity Theorem:
$$\operatorname{rank}(A) + \operatorname{nullity}(A) = n$$
where $n$ is the number of unknowns (columns of $A$).
Here $n = 6$ and $\operatorname{rank}(A) = 3$:
$$\operatorname{nullity}(A) = n - \operatorname{rank}(A) = 6 - 3 = 3$$
The nullity of $A$ represents the dimension of the solution space, which is the number of linearly independent solutions. Therefore, the answer is $3$.

questions.question: The value of the limit $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin(3x) - 3x}{x^3}$ is equal to ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
Using Taylor series expansion of $\sin(u) = u - \frac{u^3}{6} + O(u^5)$ with $u = 3x$:
$$\sin(3x) = 3x - \frac{(3x)^3}{6} + O(x^5) = 3x - \frac{27x^3}{6} + O(x^5) = 3x - \frac{9}{2}x^3 + O(x^5)$$
Subtracting $3x$:
$$\sin(3x) - 3x = -\frac{9}{2}x^3 + O(x^5)$$
Dividing by $x^3$ and taking limit $x \to 0$:
$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{-\frac{9}{2}x^3 + O(x^5)}{x^3} = -\frac{9}{2} = -4.5$$

questions.question: The primary component of a mouldboard plough that cuts the horizontal slice of soil from the furrow bottom is called the:
questions.solution:
In a mouldboard plough:
• The **share** makes the horizontal cut separating the furrow slice from the furrow floor.
• The **coulter** makes the vertical cut.
• The **mouldboard** lifts, pulverizes, and inverts the furrow slice.
• The **landside** takes the lateral side-thrust against the furrow wall.

questions.subtopic: Overload safety devices used in farm machinery
questions.question: In a PTO-driven rotary tiller (rotavator), which of the following devices is most commonly employed to protect the transmission gears against sudden overload when the tines hit a stone?
questions.solution: A spring-loaded slip clutch (friction disc torque limiter) or a shear bolt is installed on the PTO drive shaft of rotavators to slip at a predetermined torque threshold, preventing catastrophic gear or shaft failure.

questions.subtopic: Measurement of force, stress, torque, speed, displacement and acceleration on machine elements – shafts, couplings, keys, bearings and knuckle joints
questions.question: A knuckle joint connecting two tie-rods in a tractor steering linkage carries an axial tensile load of $P = 40\text{ kN}$. The joint pin has a diameter of $d = 25\text{ mm}$ and is subjected to double shear. The average shear stress induced in the pin in $\text{MPa}$ is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place). Take $\pi = 3.1416$.
questions.solution:
In a knuckle joint, the pin fails in double shear across two circular cross-sections:
$$A_s = 2 \times \left(\frac{\pi}{4} d^2\right) = \frac{\pi}{2} (25\text{ mm})^2 = 1.5708 \times 625 = 981.75\text{ mm}^2$$
$$\tau = \frac{P}{A_s} = \frac{40,000\text{ N}}{981.75\text{ mm}^2} \approx 40.74\text{ MPa} \approx 40.7\text{ MPa}$$

questions.question: For the same compression ratio $r$ and heat input, the theoretical thermal efficiencies of air-standard cycles follow the order:
questions.solution:
For identical compression ratio and identical heat addition:
$$\eta_{\text{Otto}} > \eta_{\text{Dual}} > \eta_{\text{Diesel}}$$
Because heat is added entirely at constant volume in the Otto cycle (at peak temperature), whereas in the Diesel cycle heat is added at constant pressure (as the cylinder expands, lowering expansion ratio during heat release).

questions.subtopic: Sources of power on the farm – human, animal, mechanical, electrical, wind, solar and biomass
questions.question: An agricultural worker operating a rotary pedal thresher works at a metabolic energy expenditure rate of $24.0\text{ kJ/min}$. If the human mechanical work efficiency is $20\%$ ($0.20$), the sustained mechanical power output delivered by the worker in Watts is ________ (answer in integer).
questions.solution:
1. Metabolic power expenditure ($P_{met}$):
$$P_{met} = \frac{24.0\text{ kJ/min} \times 1000\text{ J/kJ}}{60\text{ s}} = 400\text{ W}$$
2. Mechanical power output ($P_{mech}$):
$$P_{mech} = P_{met} \times \eta_{mech} = 400\text{ W} \times 0.20 = 80\text{ W}$$
(Note: An average adult agricultural laborer can sustain approximately $0.1\text{ hp} \approx 75\text{ W}$ of continuous mechanical power).

questions.question: A tractor diesel engine operates under part-load with an actual operating air-fuel ratio of $(A/F)_{act} = 22.5$. If the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio is $(A/F)_{st} = 15.0$, the fuel-air equivalence ratio ($\phi = \frac{(A/F)_{st}}{(A/F)_{act}}$) of the mixture is ________ (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
The fuel-air equivalence ratio $\phi$ is defined as:
$$\phi = \frac{(F/A)_{act}}{(F/A)_{st}} = \frac{(A/F)_{st}}{(A/F)_{act}}$$
Given $(A/F)_{st} = 15.0$ and $(A/F)_{act} = 22.5$:
$$\phi = \frac{15.0}{22.5} = \frac{2}{3} \approx 0.6667 \approx 0.67$$
(Note: $\phi < 1.0$ indicates a lean combustion mixture, typical for diesel engines).

questions.subtopic: Power transmission systems – gear trains, differential, final drives and power take-off
questions.question: The primary function of the differential lock mechanism in an agricultural tractor is to:

options.A: Increase the turning radius of the tractor during tight headland turns
options.B: Equalize the rotational speeds of both drive wheels when one wheel loses traction and spins
options.C: Disengage the PTO shaft under overload
options.D: Allow the outer wheel to rotate faster than the inner wheel during cornering

questions.solution: When one driving wheel encounters slippery mud, an open differential transfers no torque to the other wheel (it spins freely). Engaging the differential lock couples both axle shafts together so both drive wheels rotate at identical speeds with full traction.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.subtopic: Hydrograph analysis, unit hydrograph theory and application
questions.question: Which of the following fundamental assumptions underlies Sherman's Unit Hydrograph (UH) theory?

options.A: Time invariance and linear response of the watershed
options.B: Rainfall excess is non-uniformly distributed over the drainage basin
options.C: Base time of direct runoff increases proportionally with excess rainfall depth
options.D: Peak discharge is inversely proportional to effective rainfall

questions.solution:
The two classical tenets of Unit Hydrograph theory are:
1. **Linear response (Principle of Superposition & Proportionality)**: Direct runoff ordinates are directly proportional to the rainfall excess depth.
2. **Time invariance**: The catchment direct runoff response to a unit input remains constant irrespective of when the storm occurs.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: A series of closed contour lines on a topographic map having higher elevation values inside and decreasing values outwards indicates a:
questions.solution: Closed contour lines with increasing elevation towards the centre represent a hill or knoll. If elevations decrease towards the centre, it represents a depression.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: A fine-grained soil has a liquid limit $w_L = 45\%$ and a plastic limit $w_P = 22\%$. According to Casagrande's plasticity chart, the plasticity index of the A-line ($I_{P, A\text{-line}} = 0.73(w_L - 20)$) in percentage is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
The equation of the A-line in the Indian Standard / Casagrande Plasticity Chart is:
$$I_{P, A\text{-line}} = 0.73 (w_L - 20)$$
Given $w_L = 45\%$:
$$I_{P, A\text{-line}} = 0.73 (45 - 20) = 0.73 \times 25 = 18.25\% \approx 18.3\%$$

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: A triangular channel has side slopes of $1\text{ horizontal to } 1\text{ vertical}$ ($z = 1$). If the flow depth is $0.80\text{ m}$, the hydraulic radius of the section in meters is ________ (round off to 3 decimal places).
questions.solution:
For a triangular channel with side slope $z:1$:
1. Area $A = z y^2 = 1 \times (0.80)^2 = 0.64\text{ m}^2$.
2. Wetted perimeter $P = 2 y \sqrt{1 + z^2} = 2 \times 0.80 \times \sqrt{1 + 1^2} = 1.60 \sqrt{2} = 2.2627\text{ m}$.
3. Hydraulic radius $R$:
$$R = \frac{A}{P} = \frac{0.64}{2.2627} = \frac{y}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{0.80}{2.8284} \approx 0.2828\text{ m} \approx 0.283\text{ m}$$

questions.question: According to the affinity laws for a centrifugal pump with a fixed impeller diameter, if the pump rotational speed $N$ is doubled, the head $H$ developed by the pump will:
questions.solution:
Centrifugal pump affinity laws state:
1. Discharge: $Q \propto N$
2. Head: $H \propto N^2$
3. Brake Power: $P \propto N^3$
When speed is doubled ($N_2 = 2N_1$):
$$\frac{H_2}{H_1} = \left(\frac{N_2}{N_1}\right)^2 = 2^2 = 4$$

questions.topic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
questions.question: A steady water stream of $100\text{ L/s}$ is diverted from a canal outlet into an unlined field channel. The stream discharge measured at the entrance of the agricultural field is $80\text{ L/s}$. The water conveyance efficiency ($\eta_c$) of the channel expressed in percentage is ________ (answer in integer).
questions.solution:
Water conveyance efficiency is defined as:
$$\eta_c = \frac{W_f}{W_d} \times 100$$
Where:
• $W_f = 80\text{ L/s}$ (water delivered to the field plot)
• $W_d = 100\text{ L/s}$ (water diverted from the source/canal)
$$\eta_c = \frac{80}{100} \times 100 = 80\%$$

questions.question: In the design of deep grain silos, Janssen's equation demonstrates that with increasing grain depth, the lateral pressure against the silo wall:

options.B: Approaches an asymptotic maximum limiting value
options.D: Remains strictly equal to hydrostatic liquid pressure

questions.solution: Janssen's equation accounts for friction between the grain and the bin wall ($L = \frac{w R}{\mu'} [1 - e^{-k \mu' y / R}]$). As depth $y \to \infty$, the exponential term decays to zero and lateral pressure approaches an asymptotic upper limit $\frac{w R}{\mu'}$, unlike fluids which increase linearly.

questions.question: Using Siebel's equation for specific heat above freezing, $c_p = 0.837 + 3.349 M$ (where $M$ is the moisture content fraction on a wet basis), the specific heat of wheat grain at $15\%$ wet basis moisture content in $\text{kJ/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$ is ________ (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
From Siebel's formula for agricultural produce above freezing:
$$c_p = 0.837 + 3.349 M$$
Given $M = 15\% = 0.15$ wet basis:
$$c_p = 0.837 + 3.349(0.15) = 0.837 + 0.50235 = 1.33935\text{ kJ/(kg}\cdot\text{K)} \approx 1.34\text{ kJ/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$$

questions.question: During a laboratory test on a grain pile, paddy grains are discharged on a horizontal circular disc of diameter $0.60\text{ m}$. The grains form a conical heap of height $0.18\text{ m}$ covering the entire disc surface. The angle of repose of the paddy grains in degrees is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
The angle of repose $\theta$ of a conical grain heap is given by:
$$\tan \theta = \frac{h}{r}$$
Where:
• Cone height $h = 0.18\text{ m}$
• Base radius $r = \frac{0.60}{2} = 0.30\text{ m}$
$$\tan \theta = \frac{0.18}{0.30} = 0.60$$
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.60) \approx 30.9638^\circ \approx 31.0^\circ$$

questions.question: In dielectric heating of grain, the relative dielectric constant of the grain is $\epsilon' = 25.0$ and the dielectric loss factor is $\epsilon'' = 5.0$. The loss tangent (dissipation factor, $\tan \delta = \epsilon'' / \epsilon'$) of the grain is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
The loss tangent $\tan \delta$ measures the dissipation of electrical energy into heat:
$$\tan \delta = \frac{\epsilon''}{\epsilon'} = \frac{5.0}{25.0} = 0.20$$

questions.subtopic: Drying and milling of cereals, pulses and oilseeds
questions.question: In a modern rice mill, $2500\text{ kg}$ of cleaned paddy with $14\%$ moisture content is milled. The milling yields $1750\text{ kg}$ of total milled rice (including brokens), which contains $1400\text{ kg}$ of whole unbroken head rice. The Head Rice Yield ($HRY$) of the paddy expressed as a percentage of the raw paddy feed is ________ % (answer in integer).
questions.solution:
Head Rice Yield ($HRY$) is defined as:
$$HRY = \frac{\text{Mass of head rice}}{\text{Mass of rough paddy feed}} \times 100$$
$$HRY = \frac{1400\text{ kg}}{2500\text{ kg}} \times 100 = 56.0\%$$

questions.topic: Unit Operations in Dairy and Food Engineering
questions.question: The primary objective of two-stage homogenization in fluid milk processing is to:

options.A: Disrupt fat globules in the 1st stage and disperse fat globule clumps in the 2nd stage
options.B: Inactivate heat-resistant bacterial spores at high shear
options.C: Increase the creaming index of whole milk
options.D: Pasteurize the milk at low pressure

questions.solution:
In two-stage milk homogenization:
• The high-pressure first stage (approx. 15–20 MPa) breaks larger milk fat globules down to <2 microns.
• The lower-pressure second stage (approx. 3–5 MPa) breaks up fat globule clusters/clumps to ensure uniform emulsion stability and prevent creaming.

questions.subtopic: Water activity, sorption and desorption isotherms
questions.question: The difference in equilibrium moisture content of a food material between the adsorption and desorption curves at the same water activity ($a_w$) is known as:
questions.solution: At a given water activity $a_w$, the equilibrium moisture content is higher during desorption than during adsorption. This non-coincidence of curves is termed **sorption hysteresis**.

questions.question: The linear transformation $T: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ that reflects every vector about the line $y = x$ has the standard matrix representation:
questions.solution:
Under reflection across the line $y = x$:
1. The basis vector $e_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$ transforms to $T(e_1) = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$.
2. The basis vector $e_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ transforms to $T(e_2) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$.
The standard matrix is formed by these column vectors:
$$[T] = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$$
Notice that $[T]^T [T] = I$ and $\det([T]) = -1$, which confirms it is an orthogonal reflection.

questions.question: Let $A$ be a $3 \times 3$ invertible real matrix with $\det(A) = 4$. The determinant of the matrix $2 \operatorname{adj}(A)$ is ________ (answer in integer).
questions.solution:
For an $n \times n$ matrix $A$ and a scalar $k$:
$$\det(k B) = k^n \det(B)$$
Here $B = \operatorname{adj}(A)$ and $n = 3$, so:
$$\det(2 \operatorname{adj}(A)) = 2^3 \det(\operatorname{adj}(A)) = 8 \det(\operatorname{adj}(A))$$
Using the standard identity $\det(\operatorname{adj}(A)) = (\det(A))^{n-1}$ for $n = 3$:
$$\det(\operatorname{adj}(A)) = (\det(A))^{3-1} = 4^2 = 16$$
Substituting this back:
$$\det(2 \operatorname{adj}(A)) = 8 \times 16 = 128$$

questions.question: Given the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$. Using the Cayley–Hamilton theorem, the matrix expression $A^2 - 5A$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
The characteristic equation of $A$ is:
$$\det(A - \lambda I) = (1 - \lambda)(4 - \lambda) - 6 = \lambda^2 - 5\lambda - 2 = 0$$
By the Cayley–Hamilton theorem, every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation:
$$A^2 - 5A - 2I = 0$$
Rearranging terms:
$$A^2 - 5A = 2I$$
Therefore, option B is correct.

questions.question: If the equation $F(x, y, z) = 0$ defines $z$ implicitly as a function of independent variables $x$ and $y$, then provided $\frac{\partial F}{\partial z} \ne 0$, the partial derivative $\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}$ is given by:
questions.solution:
Taking the total differential of $F(x, y, z) = 0$:
$$dF = \frac{\partial F}{\partial x} dx + \frac{\partial F}{\partial y} dy + \frac{\partial F}{\partial z} dz = 0$$
To find $\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}$, hold $y$ constant ($dy = 0$):
$$\frac{\partial F}{\partial x} dx + \frac{\partial F}{\partial z} dz = 0 \implies \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} = -\frac{\partial F/\partial x}{\partial F/\partial z}$$
Hence, option A is correct.

questions.subtopic: Calculation of power, torque, fuel consumption, heat load and power losses
questions.question: A four-cylinder, four-stroke diesel engine with bore of $100\text{ mm}$ and stroke of $100\text{ mm}$ runs at $2000\text{ rpm}$. The engine develops an indicated mean effective pressure of $650\text{ kPa}$. The indicated power developed by the engine in $\text{kW}$ is ________ (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
Indicated Power formula for a multi-cylinder four-stroke engine:
$$IP = \frac{p_{imep} \cdot L \cdot A \cdot n \cdot k}{60 \times 1000}$$
Where:
• $p_{imep} = 650\text{ kPa} = 650 \times 10^3\text{ N/m}^2$
• Stroke $L = 100\text{ mm} = 0.10\text{ m}$
• Bore $D = 100\text{ mm} = 0.10\text{ m} \implies A = \frac{\pi}{4}(0.10)^2 = 0.007854\text{ m}^2$
• For 4-stroke engine, power strokes per minute $n = \frac{N}{2} = \frac{2000}{2} = 1000\text{ rpm}$
• Number of cylinders $k = 4$
$$IP = \frac{(650 \times 10^3) \times 0.10 \times 0.007854 \times 1000 \times 4}{60 \times 1000} = \frac{2042.04}{60} = 34.03\text{ kW}$$

questions.subtopic: Calculation of performance parameters – field capacity, efficiency, performance index, application rate and losses
questions.question: A 4-bottom tractor-mounted mouldboard plough has a cutting width of 35 cm per bottom. It operates at an average forward speed of $5.4\text{ km/h}$. If the field efficiency is $80\%$, the effective field capacity of the plough in $\text{ha/h}$ is ________ (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
1. Total width of cut $W$:
$$W = 4 \times 0.35\text{ m} = 1.4\text{ m}$$
2. Forward speed $S$:
$$S = 5.4\text{ km/h}$$
3. Theoretical Field Capacity ($TFC$):
$$TFC = \frac{W \times S}{10} = \frac{1.4 \times 5.4}{10} = 0.756\text{ ha/h}$$
4. Effective Field Capacity ($EFC$):
$$EFC = TFC \times \eta = 0.756 \times 0.80 = 0.6048\text{ ha/h} \approx 0.60\text{ ha/h}$$

questions.subtopic: Design and selection of machine elements – gears, pulleys, chains and sprockets and belts
questions.question: A flat belt drive connects two pulleys. The driving pulley of diameter $250\text{ mm}$ rotates at $1440\text{ rpm}$. If belt slip on each pulley is $2\%$, the rotational speed of the driven pulley of diameter $500\text{ mm}$ in $\text{rpm}$ is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
Speed ratio of belt drive considering total slip $s$:
$$\frac{N_2}{N_1} = \frac{d_1}{d_2} \left(1 - \frac{s}{100}\right)$$
Total slip $s = s_1 + s_2 = 2\% + 2\% = 4\%$.
$$N_2 = 1440 \times \frac{250}{500} \times \left(1 - \frac{4}{100}\right) = 1440 \times 0.5 \times 0.96 = 691.2\text{ rpm}$$
Acceptable range: 689.0 to 693.0 rpm.

questions.question: When operating a subsoiler or deep chisel tine to shatter a dense subsurface hardpan, if the working depth is increased beyond the 'critical depth':

options.A: Soil is no longer lifted upward in a crescent failure pattern, but is instead pushed sideways in a compacted two-dimensional plastic flow, drastically increasing specific draft without increasing surface soil shattering
options.B: Draft force becomes completely independent of working depth
options.C: Specific draft drops to zero due to spontaneous soil liquefaction
options.D: The vertical force shifts from downward suction to an uncontrollable upward thrust

questions.solution: Beyond the critical depth, soil confining pressure prevents upward crescent shear failure. The tine creates subterranean compaction grooves via lateral plastic flow, sharply increasing specific draft ($N/cm^2$) with negligible shatter benefit.

questions.question: A 2WD tractor has a total static weight of $24\text{ kN}$ with $65\%$ of the weight resting on the rear axle on level ground. The wheelbase is $2.0\text{ m}$. A horizontal pull of $8\text{ kN}$ is applied at a drawbar height of $0.45\text{ m}$ above ground. Assuming no rolling resistance on front wheels, the dynamic weight on the front wheels during pulling in $\text{kN}$ is ________ (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
1. Static front wheel weight $W_{fs}$:
$$W_{fs} = (1 - 0.65) \times 24\text{ kN} = 0.35 \times 24 = 8.40\text{ kN}$$
2. Dynamic weight transfer from front to rear axle due to horizontal drawbar pull $P$:
$$\Delta W = \frac{P \times h}{x_b}$$
Where $P = 8\text{ kN}$, drawbar hitch height $h = 0.45\text{ m}$, wheelbase $x_b = 2.0\text{ m}$.
$$\Delta W = \frac{8 \times 0.45}{2.0} = \frac{3.60}{2.0} = 1.80\text{ kN}$$
3. Dynamic load on front wheels $W_{fd}$:
$$W_{fd} = W_{fs} - \Delta W = 8.40 - 1.80 = 6.60\text{ kN}$$

questions.question: A tractor drive wheel of rolling radius $0.75\text{ m}$ completes 100 revolutions while travelling a horizontal distance of $424\text{ m}$ in tilled soil. The wheel slip expressed in percentage is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
1. Theoretical distance without slip $S_{th}$:
$$S_{th} = 2 \pi r \cdot N = 2 \times 3.14159 \times 0.75 \times 100 = 471.24\text{ m}$$
2. Actual distance travelled $S_a = 424\text{ m}$.
3. Wheel slip $s$:
$$s = \frac{S_{th} - S_a}{S_{th}} \times 100 = \frac{471.24 - 424}{471.24} \times 100 = \frac{47.24}{471.24} \times 100 = 10.02\% \approx 10.0\%$$

questions.subtopic: Power efficiencies and measurement, engine performance curves
questions.question: A tractor diesel engine develops $30\text{ kW}$ brake power while consuming $7.5\text{ kg}$ of diesel fuel per hour. The lower calorific value of the fuel is $42\text{ MJ/kg}$. The brake thermal efficiency of the engine expressed in percentage is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
1. Total heat energy supplied by fuel per second ($Q_{\text{in}}$):
$$Q_{\text{in}} = \frac{\dot{m}_f \times CV}{3600} = \frac{7.5\text{ kg/h} \times 42,000\text{ kJ/kg}}{3600\text{ s}} = \frac{315,000}{3600} = 87.5\text{ kW}$$
2. Brake power output $BP = 30\text{ kW}$.
3. Brake thermal efficiency ($\eta_{\text{bth}}$):
$$\eta_{\text{bth}} = \frac{BP}{Q_{\text{in}}} \times 100 = \frac{30}{87.5} \times 100 = 34.285\% \approx 34.3\%$$

questions.question: An ideal air-standard Otto cycle operates with a volumetric compression ratio $r = 8.0$. Assuming the adiabatic index $\gamma = 1.40$, the theoretical thermal efficiency of the cycle expressed in percentage is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
Thermal efficiency of an air-standard Otto cycle is given by:
$$\eta_{\text{Otto}} = 1 - \frac{1}{r^{\gamma - 1}}$$
Given $r = 8.0$ and $\gamma = 1.40$:
$$\gamma - 1 = 0.40$$
$$r^{0.40} = 8^{0.40} \approx 2.2974$$
$$\eta_{\text{Otto}} = 1 - \frac{1}{2.2974} = 1 - 0.43527 = 0.56473 = 56.47\% \approx 56.5\%$$

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.subtopic: Dimensional analysis – concepts of geometric dimensionless numbers
questions.question: In fluid mechanics and open channel hydraulic modeling, which dimensionless number represents the ratio of inertial force to gravitational force, governing free-surface wave propagation and hydraulic jump phenomena?
questions.solution:
- Froude number ($Fr$) represents the square root of the ratio of inertia force to gravity force ($Fr = \frac{V}{\sqrt{g L}}$). It governs all open-channel, weir, and spillway hydraulic modeling.
- Reynolds number governs viscous dissipation.
- Weber number governs surface tension phenomena (droplet breakup, thin-film aeration).
- Euler number governs pressure-gradient driven flows. Option A is correct.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: Using the Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE), $A = R \cdot K \cdot LS \cdot C \cdot P$, compute the predicted annual soil loss in $\text{t/(ha}\cdot\text{yr)}$ for a watershed with $R = 300\text{ MJ}\cdot\text{mm/(ha}\cdot\text{h}\cdot\text{yr)}$, $K = 0.04\text{ t}\cdot\text{ha}\cdot\text{h/(ha}\cdot\text{MJ}\cdot\text{mm)}$, $LS = 2.5$, crop cover factor $C = 0.20$, and conservation practice factor $P = 0.50$. Answer in integer ________.
questions.solution:
From the USLE formula:
$$A = R \times K \times LS \times C \times P$$
Substituting given parameters:
$$A = 300 \times 0.04 \times 2.5 \times 0.20 \times 0.50$$
1. $300 \times 0.04 = 12$
2. $12 \times 2.5 = 30$
3. $30 \times 0.20 = 6$
4. $6 \times 0.50 = 3\text{ t/(ha}\cdot\text{yr)}$
Hence, the predicted soil loss is 3.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: Water flows uniformly at a depth of $1.5\text{ m}$ in a rectangular concrete channel of width $4.0\text{ m}$ on a bed slope of $0.0016$. Manning's roughness coefficient $n = 0.015$. The discharge through the channel in $\text{m}^3\text{/s}$ is ________ (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
1. Flow cross-sectional area $A$:
$$A = B \times y = 4.0 \times 1.5 = 6.0\text{ m}^2$$
2. Wetted perimeter $P$:
$$P = B + 2y = 4.0 + 2(1.5) = 7.0\text{ m}$$
3. Hydraulic radius $R$:
$$R = \frac{A}{P} = \frac{6.0}{7.0} = 0.8571\text{ m}$$
4. Bed slope $S_0 = 0.0016 \implies \sqrt{S_0} = 0.04$
5. Discharge via Manning's equation:
$$Q = \frac{1}{n} A R^{2/3} S_0^{1/2} = \frac{1}{0.015} \times 6.0 \times (0.8571)^{2/3} \times 0.04$$
$$(0.8571)^{2/3} \approx 0.9023$$
$$Q = 400 \times 6.0 \times 0.9023 \times 0.04 = 2400 \times 0.04 \times 0.9023 = 19.38\text{ m}^3\text{/s}$$

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.subtopic: Flow through orifices, weirs and notches
questions.question: For flow issuing through a sharp-crested circular orifice under a constant hydraulic head, the coefficient of discharge ($C_d$) is related to the coefficient of velocity ($C_v$) and coefficient of contraction ($C_c$) by which fundamental relationship?
questions.solution:
Actual discharge $Q_{act} = A_{act} \times V_{act}$.
Theoretical discharge $Q_{th} = A_{th} \times V_{th}$.
By definition:
$$C_c = \frac{A_{act}}{A_{th}} \quad \text{and} \quad C_v = \frac{V_{act}}{V_{th}}$$
$$C_d = \frac{Q_{act}}{Q_{th}} = \frac{A_{act} V_{act}}{A_{th} V_{th}} = C_c \times C_v$$
Option A is correct.

questions.question: A crop with a root zone depth of $80\text{ cm}$ is grown on a sandy loam soil. The field capacity and permanent wilting point of the soil on a dry weight basis are $22\%$ and $10\%$, respectively. The apparent specific gravity of the dry soil is $1.50$. If irrigation is to be applied when $50\%$ of available soil water is depleted, the net irrigation requirement in $\text{mm}$ is ________ (answer in integer).
questions.solution:
1. Available water capacity ($AWC$):
$$AWC = \frac{\rho_b}{\rho_w} \cdot d \cdot (FC - PWP)$$
Where:
• Apparent specific gravity $\frac{\rho_b}{\rho_w} = 1.50$
• Root zone depth $d = 80\text{ cm} = 800\text{ mm}$
• Field capacity $FC = 0.22$
• Permanent wilting point $PWP = 0.10$
$$AWC = 1.50 \times 800 \times (0.22 - 0.10) = 1200 \times 0.12 = 144\text{ mm}$$
2. Net irrigation requirement ($NIR$) at $50\%$ allowable depletion:
$$NIR = 0.50 \times AWC = 0.50 \times 144 = 72\text{ mm}$$

questions.topic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
questions.subtopic: Surface, sprinkler and micro irrigation methods
questions.question: Which of the following statements concerning micro-irrigation (drip irrigation) systems are correct?

options.A: Operating pressure at the emitter nozzles typically ranges between $100\text{ kPa}$ and $200\text{ kPa}$ ($1\text{ to }2\text{ bar}$).
options.B: Pressure-compensating (PC) emitters maintain an approximately constant discharge despite lateral elevation changes and pipe friction losses.
options.C: Emitter orifice clogging from physical particulates, chemical salt precipitation, and biological growth is the primary operational hazard.
options.D: Water application efficiency in drip irrigation is lower than that in surface border irrigation due to excessive wet-bulb surface evaporation.

questions.solution:
• Drip systems operate at low pressure heads, typically 100–200 kPa (A is correct).
• PC emitters use flexible elastomeric diaphragms to maintain uniform discharge across varying pressures (B is correct).
• Emitter clogging is universally recognized as the primary operational vulnerability of micro-irrigation (C is correct).
• Drip application efficiency is exceptionally high (90–95%), far superior to surface irrigation (D is incorrect).

questions.subtopic: Steady and unsteady flow in confined and unconfined aquifers
questions.question: A fully penetrating well of radius $0.20\text{ m}$ taps a confined aquifer of thickness $20\text{ m}$. Hydraulic conductivity of the aquifer is $15\text{ m/day}$. During pumping, the steady state drawdowns measured at radial distances of $10\text{ m}$ and $50\text{ m}$ from the well centre are $3.0\text{ m}$ and $1.0\text{ m}$, respectively. The steady pumping discharge $Q$ in $\text{m}^3\text{/day}$ is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place). Take $\pi = 3.1416$.
questions.solution:
For steady radial flow in a confined aquifer (Thiem's equation):
$$Q = \frac{2 \pi K b (s_1 - s_2)}{\ln(r_2 / r_1)}$$
Where:
• $K = 15\text{ m/day}$
• Confined aquifer thickness $b = 20\text{ m}$
• Drawdown $s_1 = 3.0\text{ m}$ at $r_1 = 10\text{ m}$
• Drawdown $s_2 = 1.0\text{ m}$ at $r_2 = 50\text{ m}$
• $s_1 - s_2 = 3.0 - 1.0 = 2.0\text{ m}$
• $\ln(r_2/r_1) = \ln(50/10) = \ln(5) \approx 1.6094$
$$Q = \frac{2 \times 3.1416 \times 15 \times 20 \times 2.0}{1.6094} = \frac{3769.9}{1.6094} \approx 1172.5\text{ m}^3\text{/day}$$

questions.question: An agricultural drainage basin has an area of $500\text{ ha}$. The design drainage coefficient is $12\text{ mm/day}$. The continuous design drainage discharge required to remove this excess water in $\text{m}^3\text{/s}$ is ________ (round off to 3 decimal places).
questions.solution:
1. Area $A = 500\text{ ha} = 500 \times 10^4\text{ m}^2 = 5 \times 10^6\text{ m}^2$.
2. Drainage coefficient $D_c = 12\text{ mm/day} = 0.012\text{ m/day}$.
3. Daily volume $V = A \times D_c = (5 \times 10^6) \times 0.012 = 60,000\text{ m}^3\text{/day}$.
4. Discharge in $\text{m}^3\text{/s}$:
$$Q = \frac{60,000}{24 \times 3600} = \frac{60,000}{86,400} = 0.6944\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \approx 0.694\text{ m}^3\text{/s}$$

questions.question: In membrane separation processes for liquid foods, as the molecular weight cut-off (MWCO) decreases from Microfiltration (MF) to Ultrafiltration (UF), Nanofiltration (NF), and Reverse Osmosis (RO):

options.A: The pore size decreases and the required hydraulic operating pressure increases
options.B: The pore size increases and the operating pressure decreases
options.C: The osmotic pressure difference across the membrane approaches zero
options.D: The permeation flux of pure water increases exponentially

questions.solution: Across the membrane spectrum from MF to RO, effective pore size decreases from micrometers down to sub-nanometers (<1 nm). To overcome the tighter membrane resistance and significantly higher osmotic pressures of retained low-molecular solutes, the required hydraulic driving pressure increases from ~1 bar up to 40–80 bar.

questions.subtopic: Drying and milling of cereals, pulses and oilseeds
questions.question: A batch of $1000\text{ kg}$ of wet paddy at $25\%$ moisture content (wet basis) is dried to $14\%$ moisture content (wet basis). The amount of water removed during drying in $\text{kg}$ is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
1. Bone dry matter in initial wet paddy ($W_1 = 1000\text{ kg}$, $M_1 = 25\%$ w.b.):
$$DM = W_1 \times (1 - M_1) = 1000 \times (1 - 0.25) = 750\text{ kg}$$
2. Dry matter remains constant during drying. Final mass $W_2$ at $M_2 = 14\%$ w.b.:
$$DM = W_2 \times (1 - M_2)$$
$$W_2 = \frac{750}{1 - 0.14} = \frac{750}{0.86} = 872.09\text{ kg}$$
3. Mass of water removed $\Delta W$:
$$\Delta W = W_1 - W_2 = 1000 - 872.09 = 127.91\text{ kg} \approx 127.9\text{ kg}$$

questions.question: Which of the following factors significantly influence the screening effectiveness and capacity of vibratory grain cleaners?

options.A: Sieve slope and stroke length of vibration
options.B: Frequency of oscillation and angle of throw

questions.solution: Screening effectiveness is governed by the physical motion parameters (slope, amplitude, frequency, angle of vibration) and feed material characteristics (moisture content affecting agglomeration and blinding). The structural paint color of the frame has no mechanical impact.

questions.subtopic: Mechanics and energy requirement in size reduction of agriculture produce
questions.question: According to Rittinger's law of comminution, the energy required to grind a material from an average feed diameter $L_1 = 10\text{ mm}$ to product diameter $L_2 = 2\text{ mm}$ is $12\text{ kJ/kg}$. The energy required in $\text{kJ/kg}$ to grind the same material from feed diameter $10\text{ mm}$ to product diameter $1\text{ mm}$ is ________ (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution:
Rittinger's law states that energy $E$ is proportional to new surface area created:
$$E = K_R \left( \frac{1}{L_2} - \frac{1}{L_1} \right)$$
For the first reduction ($L_1 = 10\text{ mm}$, $L_2 = 2\text{ mm}$):
$$12 = K_R \left( \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{10} \right) = K_R (0.5 - 0.1) = 0.4 K_R \implies K_R = \frac{12}{0.4} = 30$$
For the second reduction ($L_1 = 10\text{ mm}$, $L_2' = 1\text{ mm}$):
$$E' = 30 \left( \frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{10} \right) = 30 (1 - 0.1) = 30 \times 0.9 = 27.0\text{ kJ/kg}$$

questions.subtopic: Kinetics of microbial death – pasteurization and sterilization of milk and other liquid foods
questions.question: A bacterial spore suspension has a decimal reduction time ($D_{121}$ value) of $1.5\text{ minutes}$ at $121^\circ\text{C}$. The thermal holding time in minutes required at $121^\circ\text{C}$ to achieve a $12\text{-D}$ reduction of this bacterial population is ________ (answer in integer).
questions.solution:
The thermal death time $F$ for an $n$-decimal reduction is:
$$F = n \times D$$
Given:
• Decimal reduction time $D = 1.5\text{ minutes}$
• Number of log reductions $n = 12$
$$F = 12 \times 1.5\text{ min} = 18\text{ minutes}$$

questions.subtopic: Kinetics of microbial death – pasteurization and sterilization of milk and other liquid foods
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding thermal processing parameters ($D$, $z$, and $F$ values) is/are correct?

options.A: The $D$-value is the heating time required at a given temperature to destroy $90\%$ of a microbial population.
options.B: The $z$-value represents the temperature increase required to reduce the $D$-value by a factor of 10.
options.C: A higher $z$-value indicates higher temperature sensitivity of the microorganism.
options.D: The standard reference temperature for calculating $F_0$ value in thermal sterilization of low-acid foods is $121.1^\circ\text{C}$ ($250^\circ\text{F}$).

questions.solution:
• $D$-value is time for 1-log (90%) reduction (A is correct).
• $z$-value is temperature change required for a 1-decade change in $D$-value (B is correct).
• A lower $z$-value implies that a smaller temperature rise causes a tenfold drop in $D$-value, meaning GREATER temperature sensitivity (so C is incorrect).
• $F_0$ is defined at reference temperature $121.1^\circ\text{C}$ ($250^\circ\text{F}$) with $z = 10^\circ\text{C}$ (D is correct).

questions.question: In a counter-flow double pipe heat exchanger, milk is heated from $20^\circ\text{C}$ to $60^\circ\text{C}$ while hot water cools from $90^\circ\text{C}$ to $50^\circ\text{C}$. The Log Mean Temperature Difference (LMTD) in $^\circ\text{C}$ is ________ (answer in integer).
questions.solution:
For counter-flow arrangement:
• Inlet temperature difference $\Delta T_1 = T_{h,in} - T_{c,out} = 90^\circ\text{C} - 60^\circ\text{C} = 30^\circ\text{C}$
• Outlet temperature difference $\Delta T_2 = T_{h,out} - T_{c,in} = 50^\circ\text{C} - 20^\circ\text{C} = 30^\circ\text{C}$
When $\Delta T_1 = \Delta T_2 = \Delta T$, the LMTD is simply:
$$\text{LMTD} = \Delta T_1 = \Delta T_2 = 30^\circ\text{C}$$
